claim: E3M8, the prettiest dense Blood map, is not bigger than a plain one but denser: 34.2 sectors per 100 square bodies (E1M1 13.3); median wall run 1.33 body widths (E1M1 the same); 40 wall tiles (E1M1 40) including a tier of narrow tiles (93 and 115, read as pilasters, 32x128; 479, the owner's stone column, 32x128; 195, his jamb-face metal track, 16x128) and thin bands (6, his kerb, 64x8; 200, his riveted metal threshold, 32x16); median shade step between neighbours 2 (p95 31); 27% of sectors sloped; 52 floor levels within 6.3 bodies of range.
evidence: knowledge/blood/design/e3m8-reference-v1.json (2026-08-27), with E1M1 as control; our candidate: wall run 3.00, 17 tiles, shade step 7, 2% slopes.
use: Segment long walls first (field / pilaster / field with bloodmap.layout.Run) so trim has somewhere to sit; then shade gradually and add small level changes.
